areas.n: Sapporo (Ōdōri · Susukino · Nijō Market · Maruyama · Moiwa · Jōzankei)
Otaru & Shakotan (canal · Sushi-ya Dōri · Yoichi Nikka · Shakotan uni)
Niseko & Yōtei (Niseko · Kutchan · Rusutsu · Makkari · Kyōgoku)
Hakodate & Dōnan (Morning Market · Goryōkaku · Mt Hakodate · Motomachi · Ōnuma · Matsumae)
Shikotsu-Tōya & Iburi (Noboribetsu Jigokudani · Lake Tōya · Upopoy · Shiraoi · Tomakomai)
Dōhoku — Central Hokkaido (Asahikawa · Biei · Furano · Daisetsuzan · Sōunkyō)
Dōtō — Eastern Hokkaido (Kushiro · Akan · Mashū · Shiretoko · Abashiri · Nemuro)
Far North (Wakkanai · Cape Sōya · Rishiri · Rebun)

P.n: Sapporo Clock Tower (札幌市時計台)
P.ad: Kita 1-jo Nishi 2-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0001, Japan
P.w: The 1878 wooden drill hall of the Sapporo Agricultural College, its clock still striking the hours — the city's symbol and an Important Cultural Property.

P.n: Former Hokkaido Government Office (Akarenga, 赤れんが庁舎)
P.ad: Kita 3-jo Nishi 6-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-8588, Japan
P.w: The 1888 neo-baroque red-brick seat of the Hokkaido Development Commission — reopened 25 July 2025 after a multi-year restoration as a museum of Hokkaido history with a free garden.

P.ad: Ōdōri Nishi 1–12-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0042, Japan
P.w: The 1.5 km green firebreak that splits Sapporo north from south — stage of the Sapporo Snow Festival in February, beer gardens and the autumn food festival.

P.ad: 1-1 Moerenuma-kōen, Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 007-0011, Japan
P.w: Isamu Noguchi's last great work: a former landfill sculpted into one park-sized artwork — Mt Moere, the Glass Pyramid, the Sea Fountain.

P.n: Historical Village of Hokkaido (北海道開拓の村)
P.ad: 50-1 Konopporo, Atsubetsu-chō, Atsubetsu-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 004-0006, Japan
P.w: Open-air museum of 50-plus relocated Meiji–early Shōwa buildings — herring lodges, farmhouses, a horse-drawn tram — telling the story of Hokkaido's settlement.

P.n: Sapporo Hitsujigaoka Observation Hill (さっぽろ羊ヶ丘展望台)
P.ad: 1 Hitsujigaoka, Toyohira-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 062-0045, Japan
P.w: The hill with the bronze of Dr William S. Clark pointing to the horizon ('Boys, be ambitious!') over sheep pasture and the Ishikari Plain.

P.ad: Moiwayama, Minami-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Ropeway and mini-cable car to a 531 m summit for one of Japan's 'new three great night views' over the Sapporo grid.

P.ad: 474 Miyagaoka, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 064-8505, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's principal Shinto shrine in the Maruyama primeval forest, founded 1869 for the island's pioneer deities — cherry and plum blossom in spring.

P.n: Sapporo TV Tower (さっぽろテレビ塔)
P.ad: Ōdōri Nishi 1-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0042, Japan
P.w: The 147 m 1957 tower at the head of Ōdōri Park — the 90 m deck looks straight down the park's length.

P.n: Sapporo Beer Museum (サッポロビール博物館)
P.ad: Kita 7-jo Higashi 9-chome 1-1, Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 065-8633, Japan
P.w: Japan's only beer museum, in the 1890 red-brick Sapporo Sugar Company building — the story of the oldest Japanese beer brand, with a tasting salon.

P.n: Hokkaido University Botanic Garden (北海道大学植物園)
P.ad: Kita 3-jo Nishi 8-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0003, Japan
P.w: A 13 ha 1886 garden in the middle of downtown — native Hokkaido flora, Ainu ethnographic collection and the Miyabe memorial.

P.ad: Jōzankei Onsen, Minami-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 061-2302, Japan
P.w: Sapporo's own hot-spring town an hour south, in a Toyohira River gorge inside Shikotsu-Tōya National Park — foot baths and autumn colour.

P.ad: Minato-machi, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1923 freight canal lined with stone warehouses and gas lamps — Otaru's postcard, best at dusk and during the February Snow Light Path.

P.ad: Sakaimachi, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The preserved Meiji–Taishō merchant street a short walk from the canal — glass workshops, music boxes, LeTAO and Kitakaro sweet shops.

P.n: Otaru Music Box Museum (小樽オルゴール堂)
P.ad: 1-2-3 Irifune, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1912 brick main hall at the foot of Sakaimachi, packed with thousands of music boxes — the Vancouver-gifted steam clock whistles out front. Free entry.

P.n: Nikka Whisky Yoichi Distillery (ニッカウヰスキー余市蒸溜所)
P.ad: Kurokawa-chō, Yoichi, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Masataka Taketsuru's 1934 distillery, chosen because Yoichi most resembled Scotland — coal-fired pot stills, stone kilns and a tasting hall.

P.n: Otaru City General Museum (小樽市総合博物館)
P.ad: Temiya, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's railway birthplace — steam locomotives in the old Temiya roundhouse, plus the canal-side annex in a former warehouse.

P.ad: Goryōkaku-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's first Western-style fortress, the 1866 star fort where the Republic of Ezo made its last stand — a thousand cherry trees fill the moats in spring.

P.ad: Hakodateyama, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 334 m peak at the tip of the peninsula: a three-minute ropeway to one of Japan's great night views, the city lights pinched between two bays.

P.ad: Motomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The slope-side former foreign settlement — churches, the Old British Consulate, the Chinese Memorial Hall and the Old Public Hall of Hakodate Ward on stepped streets down to the harbour.

P.n: Hakodate Orthodox Church (Holy Resurrection, ハリストス正教会)
P.ad: Motomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's first Orthodox parish (consecrated 1860); the 1916 white church with green copper domes is an Important Cultural Property.

P.ad: Wakamatsu-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 250-odd stalls across the street from Hakodate Station — squid you fish yourself, crab, uni and ikura donburi for breakfast.

P.ad: Matsushiro, Matsumae, Matsumae District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's northernmost castle, seat of the only Edo-period domain on Hokkaido — its park is one of the island's great cherry-blossom spots, thousands of trees in 250 varieties.

P.n: Upopoy — National Ainu Museum & Park (ウポポイ)
P.ad: Wakakusa-chō, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's national centre for Ainu culture on Lake Poroto — the museum, a kotan of chise houses, dance, music and Ainu cooking.

P.ad: Noboribetsu Onsen-chō, Noboribetsu, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'Hell Valley' above Hokkaido's most famous onsen town — a steaming crater of sulphur vents feeding nine kinds of spring water, boardwalk to Oyunuma.

P.ad: Tōyako Onsen, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Round caldera lake with an island at its heart and Mount Usu steaming on its shore — onsen town, summer fireworks every night.

P.ad: Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Active volcano that last erupted in 2000 — the Usuzan Ropeway rises to crater rims and views over Lake Tōya and Shōwa-shinzan.

P.ad: Shikotsuko Onsen, Chitose, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's northernmost ice-free lake and one of its deepest and clearest — a caldera ringed by volcanoes an hour from Sapporo.

P.ad: Higashi-Asahikawa-chō Kuranuma, Asahikawa, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The zoo that reinvented Japanese zoos with behavioural exhibits — penguin parade in the snow, polar bears and seals in see-through tubes.

P.ad: Shirogane, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: An accidental pond behind a volcanic-mudflow dam whose aluminium-rich water turns an unreal cobalt around drowned larches.

P.ad: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Onsen town in a 100 m-cliffed gorge of the Ishikari River — Ginga and Ryūsei falls, and the Kurodake ropeway into Daisetsuzan.

P.ad: Asahidake Onsen, Higashikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's highest peak (2,291 m) in Daisetsuzan National Park — a ropeway to steaming fumaroles and alpine tundra, Japan's first autumn colour.

P.ad: Onnebetsu, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Five forest lakes under the Shiretoko range inside the UNESCO World Natural Heritage site — an 800 m bear-proof elevated boardwalk plus guided ground trails.

P.ad: Iwaobetsu, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'The Maiden's Tears' — groundwater seeping straight out of a sea cliff into the Sea of Okhotsk, twenty minutes' walk from the Shiretoko Nature Center.

P.n: Oshinkoshin Falls (オシンコシンの滝)
P.ad: Chashikotsu, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Twin-stream roadside falls on the way to Utoro, one of Japan's 100 best waterfalls, with a stair up to the mid-fall viewpoint.

P.ad: Shiretoko-tōge, between Utoro (Shari) and Rausu, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 738 m road pass across the peninsula, facing Mount Rausu and, across the strait, Kunashiri Island; open roughly May to early November.

P.ad: Teshikaga, Kawakami District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The Ainu 'Lake of the Gods': a 212 m-deep caldera with no inlet or outlet, famous for 'Mashū blue' clarity — and its fogs.

P.ad: Akanko Onsen, Akan-chō, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Crater lake under Me-Akan and O-Akan, home of the spherical marimo algae, with the Akankohan onsen town on its shore.

P.ad: Teshikaga, Kawakami District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's largest caldera lake — hot sand you dig into at Sunayu, open-air shore baths and winter swans.

P.ad: Kawayu Onsen, Teshikaga, Kawakami District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The Ainu 'naked mountain': a bare, yellow-crusted active volcano hissing sulphur steam beside Kawayu Onsen.

P.n: Abashiri Prison Museum (博物館 網走監獄)
P.ad: Yobito, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The Meiji prison that built Hokkaido's roads, rebuilt as an open-air museum — the five-winged radial cell block, court, bathhouse and punishment cells.

P.n: Kushiro Marsh — Kushiro-shitsugen National Park (釧路湿原)
P.ad: Hosooka Observatory (細岡展望台), Kushiro-chō, Kushiro District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's largest wetland and first Ramsar site (1980) — the stronghold of the red-crowned crane, seen from the Hosooka and marsh observatories.

P.n: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses (金森赤レンガ倉庫)
P.ad: Suehiro-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 1909 harbour warehouses (founded 1887) turned shops, beer hall and event space in 1988 — Hakodate's waterfront landmark.

P.n: Ōnuma Quasi-National Park (大沼国定公園)
P.ad: Ōnuma-chō, Nanae, Kameda District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Island-dotted Ōnuma and Konuma ponds under the volcano Hokkaidō-Komagatake — 126 islets linked by bridges, boating and cycling 30 minutes from Hakodate.

P.ad: Sōyamisaki, Wakkanai, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The northernmost point you can stand on in Japan — the triangular monument, Sakhalin on the horizon on a clear day.

P.n: Rishiri Island & Mount Rishiri (利尻島・利尻山)
P.ad: Rishiri / Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A dormant 1,721 m volcano rising straight from the sea — 'Rishiri-Fuji' — ringed by a cycling road and kelp-drying beaches; ferry from Wakkanai.

P.ad: Rebun, Rebun District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 'floating island of flowers' — alpine flowers found nowhere else bloom at sea level June–August along the Momoiwa and Cape Sukoton trails.

P.n: Taushubetsu River Bridge (タウシュベツ川橋梁)
P.ad: Nukabira, Kamishihoro, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1937 concrete arch viaduct of the abandoned Shihoro Line in Lake Nukabira — the 'phantom bridge' that surfaces and sinks with the reservoir; Japan Heritage.

P.ad: Shikaribetsu-kohan, Shikaoi, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's highest lake (810 m) and the only natural lake in Daisetsuzan National Park — canoeing in summer, an ice village with lake-ice onsen in winter.

P.n: Kōfuku Station (旧国鉄広尾線 幸福駅)
P.ad: Kōfuku-chō Higashi 1-sen, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The closed Hiroo Line halt whose name means 'happiness' — the 'Ai-koku → Kōfuku' (from Love Country to Happiness) ticket made it a pilgrimage; old railcars and ticket-covered walls remain.

P.n: Rokkatei Art Village Nakasatsunai (六花亭 中札内美術村)
P.ad: Sakae-Higashi, Nakasatsunai, Kasai District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rokkatei's oak-forest art village — four small museums, the sweets maker's restaurant and paths on old railway sleepers; free, late April–early November.

P.ad: Inada-chō Higashi 2-sen, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's first conifer garden — 83,000 m² of Japanese, Western and landscape gardens with thousands of trees from Northern Europe and Canada; on the Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.n: Tokachi Millennium Forest (十勝千年の森)
P.ad: Haobi, Shimizu, Kamikawa District (Tokachi), Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A forest planned to last a thousand years, with Dan Pearson's Earth, Meadow, Forest and Farm gardens — horse trekking and Segway tours; Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.ad: Nishi 3-sen, Nakasatsunai, Kasai District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rokkatei's 100,000 m² meadow of the 'Tokachi six flowers' painted on its wrapping paper, with small galleries of botanical art; Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.ad: Kutchan / Makkari / Kyōgoku / Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'Ezo-Fuji' — a near-perfect 1,898 m stratovolcano towering over the Niseko ski fields; its snowmelt feeds the Fukidashi springs.

P.ad: Kisen-kita, Nakafurano, Sorachi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The farm that kept Furano's lavender alive and made it famous — July's purple slopes and the striped 'Irodori' flower field under the Tokachi range. Free entry.

P.n: Ōkurayama Ski Jump Stadium & Sapporo Olympic Museum (大倉山ジャンプ競技場)
P.ad: Miyanomori, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1972 Winter Olympics large hill — ride the chairlift to the top-of-jump observatory over the city, then the Olympic Museum at its foot.

P.n: Shiroi Koibito Park (白い恋人パーク)
P.ad: Miyanosawa 2-jō, Nishi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Ishiya's Tudor-style chocolate factory behind Hokkaido's most famous souvenir cookie — factory line views, cookie workshops, a free courtyard and café.

P.ad: Minami 3-jō Higashi 1–2-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A city block of crab, uni, ikura and fish stalls since the Meiji era, with kaisendon counters and the Noren Yokochō drinking alley.

P.ad: Minami 4-jō – Minami 7-jō Nishi 2–6-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's biggest entertainment district north of Tokyo — the Nikka neon man, Ramen Yokochō, izakaya towers and the February ice-sculpture site.

P.n: Sapporo Curb Market — Jōgai Shijō (札幌場外市場)
P.ad: Kita 11-jō Nishi 21–22-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Around 60 stalls and seafood diners on the edge of the Central Wholesale Market — early-morning crab and kaisendon away from the downtown crowds.

P.n: Tanukikōji Shopping Street (狸小路商店街)
P.ad: Minami 2/3-jō Nishi 1–7-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's oldest shopping arcade (1873) — seven covered blocks of drugstores, souvenir shops, retro diners and the market at 7-chōme.

P.n: Bank of Japan Otaru Museum (日本銀行旧小樽支店金融資料館)
P.ad: 1-11-16 Ironai, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Tatsuno Kingo's 1912 branch of the Bank of Japan from the days Otaru was 'the Wall Street of the North' — now a free museum of money and the vault.

P.ad: Mogamicho, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Otaru's 532 m house mountain — a ropeway to a night view over the harbour and Ishikari Bay, and a ski hill in winter.

P.ad: Shukutsu, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A late-19th-century herring fishermen's lodge on the Shukutsu headland — the boss's quarters and bunk lofts from the herring boom that built Otaru.

P.n: Former Aoyama Villa — Otaru Kihinkan (小樽貴賓館 旧青山別邸)
P.ad: Shukutsu, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The opulent 1923 retreat a herring-fishing dynasty built from its fortune — painted ceilings, lacquer and a peony garden.

P.ad: Kamuimisaki, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: An 80 m knife-edge cape on the Shakotan Peninsula — the 'Charenka trail' ridge walk to the lighthouse above 'Shakotan blue' sea.

P.ad: Iridomari, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Through a short hand-dug tunnel to a cove of startling clear blue — one of Japan's '100 best beaches'.

P.ad: Shinsei Daisan, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Biei's biggest flower hill — around 30 kinds of flowers in stripes over the rolling fields, with the Tokachi range behind.

P.ad: Shirogane Onsen, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Groundwater spilling from a cliff into the blue Biei River at Shirogane Onsen — the 'white beard' that tints the Blue Pond downstream.

P.n: Patchwork Road, Biei (パッチワークの路)
P.ad: Biei (northwest of the town centre), Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The quilt of wheat, potato and buckwheat fields made famous by TV ads — the Ken & Mary Tree, Seven Stars Tree and Hokusei Hill lookout.

P.ad: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'Milky Way Falls', the slender twin of Ryūsei ('Shooting Star') Falls, ribboning down the 100 m basalt walls of the gorge.

P.ad: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Ropeway and chairlift from Sōunkyō to within an hour of the 1,984 m summit — the quickest way into Daisetsuzan's alpine plateau.

P.ad: Ōfune-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A Middle Jōmon village above the Pacific — more than 100 pit-dwelling hollows, some 2 m deep, part of the 2021 UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan.

P.ad: Usujiri-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A settlement where living and burial grounds were separated for millennia, with a 190 m U-shaped earthen mound; the Hakodate Jōmon Culture Center (with Hokkaido's only National Treasure, a hollow clay dogū) is beside it. UNESCO.

P.ad: Washinoki-chō, Mori, Kayabe District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's largest stone circle (Late Jōmon), a double ring of stones on a hill above Uchiura Bay — an associated site of the Jōmon World Heritage nomination.

P.n: Kitakogane Shell Mound — Jōmon (北黄金貝塚)
P.ad: Kitakogane-chō, Date, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A Jōmon settlement with large shell middens facing Uchiura Bay and a 'water site' where tools were ritually sent back — UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

P.n: Irie & Takasago Shell Mounds — Jōmon (入江・高砂貝塚)
P.ad: Takasago-chō, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Two Jōmon sites a few hundred metres apart above Uchiura Bay — the Irie village shell mound and the Takasago burial ground. UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

P.n: Kiusu Earthwork Burial Circles — Jōmon (キウス周堤墓群)
P.ad: Chitose, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Ring-shaped earthen burial enclosures up to 75 m across in a Chitose forest — among the largest Jōmon communal cemeteries. UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

P.ad: Sōbetsu Onsen, Sōbetsu, Usu District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: One of the world's youngest mountains: a lava dome that rose out of a wheat field in 1943–45 to 398 m and still steams — beside the Usuzan Ropeway base.

P.ad: Noboribetsu Onsen-chō, Noboribetsu, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A near-perfectly round caldera lake above Noboribetsu Onsen with no inflowing river — rated among Japan's clearest.

P.n: Niseko Annupuri (ニセコアンヌプリ)
P.ad: Niseko / Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1,308 m volcano whose flanks carry the Niseko United ski areas (Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village, Annupuri) — famed for deep, dry powder and backcountry gates.

P.ad: Maeda, Kyōwa, Iwanai District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The loveliest of the Niseko range's marsh ponds — a 20-minute boardwalk through alpine bog to still water ringed by Todo firs.

P.n: Fukidashi Park, Kyōgoku (ふきだし公園)
P.ad: Kyōgoku, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Mount Yōtei's snowmelt gushes out here after decades underground — one of Japan's biggest spring discharges; locals fill bottles at the source.

P.n: Sushiya-dōri — Otaru Sushi Street (寿司屋通り)
P.ad: Hanazono 1-chōme – Ironai, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: From Otaru Station toward Ironai: five or six big sushi houses and nearly twenty around them — Otaru has over a hundred places serving sushi.

P.n: Sapporo Maruyama Zoo (札幌市円山動物園)
P.ad: Miyagaoka, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Opened 1951 beside the Maruyama primeval forest — polar bears seen from an underwater tunnel, a new elephant house and Hokkaido wildlife.

P.ad: Miyagaoka, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The city's favourite hanami park at the foot of Mount Maruyama, beside Hokkaido Shrine — barbecue under the cherries in early May, red maples in autumn.

P.n: Hōheikan & Nakajima Park (豊平館・中島公園)
P.ad: Nakajima-kōen, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1880 white-and-ultramarine Western-style imperial guesthouse, an Important Cultural Property, in the downtown park with Shōbu pond, the Hassōan teahouse and Kitara concert hall.

P.n: Sapporo Art Park (札幌芸術の森)
P.ad: Geijutsu-no-mori, Minami-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 40-ha forest campus with a sculpture garden of 70-plus outdoor works, the art museum and craft studios — glorious in autumn colour.

P.n: Takino Suzuran Hillside National Government Park (国営滝野すずらん丘陵公園)
P.ad: Takino, Minami-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's only national government park — flower hills, the Ashiribetsu waterfall and forest trails, a snow park in winter.

P.n: Old Public Hall of Hakodate Ward (旧函館区公会堂)
P.ad: Motomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (top of Motoizaka slope)
P.w: The blue-grey and yellow 1910 colonial-style assembly hall looking over the port from the top of Motoizaka — an Important Cultural Property.

P.n: Former British Consulate of Hakodate (函館市旧イギリス領事館)
P.ad: Motomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The British consulate building of Hakodate's treaty-port era in Motomachi, now a city-run museum of the port's opening.

P.ad: Goryōkaku-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The observation tower beside the fort — the only way to see Goryōkaku's five-pointed star from above.

P.ad: Goryōkaku Park, Goryōkaku-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Built by the Edo shogunate in the late Edo period inside Goryōkaku to oversee northern defence and foreign affairs; restored on its original site.

P.ad: Motomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The straight, stone-curbed slope that runs from Motomachi straight down to the harbour — Hakodate's most photographed view, lit up in winter.

P.ad: Akan-chō, Ashoro, Ashoro District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: One of Hokkaido's 'three mystical lakes' at the western edge of Akan-Mashū — its colour shifts with the light under the volcano Me-Akan, whose lava dammed it.

P.ad: Route 243, Bihoro / Teshikaga border, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 525 m pass on Route 243 with the widest view over Lake Kussharo, Japan's largest caldera lake — sea of clouds at dawn.

P.ad: Kiyosato, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan (forest NE of Lake Mashū)
P.w: 'Child of the Gods' pond, fed underground from Lake Mashū — 12,000 tonnes a day of cobalt spring water that never freezes, sunken logs visible 5 m down.

P.n: Okhotsk Drift Ice Museum & Mt Tento Observatory (オホーツク流氷館)
P.ad: Mt Tento summit, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Real drift ice in a sub-zero room and a 360° rooftop view over the Sea of Okhotsk from the top of Mt Tento.

P.ad: Nosappu, Nemuro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The easternmost point of Hokkaido's mainland at the tip of the Nemuro Peninsula — Japan's earliest sunrise, looking out toward the Habomai islets.

P.ad: Notsuke, Betsukai / Shibetsu, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A long, hooked sand spit curling into the Nemuro Strait — ghostly salt-killed forests, seals and wildflowers.

P.n: Wakkanai Port North Breakwater Dome (稚内港北防波堤ドーム)
P.ad: Kaiun, Wakkanai, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 14 m-high arcade of columns built over five years to shelter travellers walking between the harbour and the railway station from waves and northern winds — a Hokkaido Heritage.

P.n: Sōya Hills & the White Road (宗谷丘陵)
P.ad: Sōya, Wakkanai, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hills shaped in the last Ice Age behind Cape Sōya, rich in wild birds and alpine plants — the 'White Road' is paved with crushed scallop shells.

P.ad: Funadomari, Rebun, Rebun District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rebun's northernmost point and trailhead of the island's 4- and 8-hour coastal hikes.

P.n: Momoiwa Observatory & Trail, Rebun (桃岩展望台)
P.ad: Motochi, Rebun, Rebun District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 'peach rock' dome above Motochi — alpine flowers with Rishiri-Fuji across the water along the ridge trail.

P.ad: Oshidomari, Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A small pond in primeval forest whose still surface mirrors Rishiri-Fuji upside down — an 800 m boardwalk loop.

P.n: Ningle Terrace, Furano (ニングルテラス)
P.ad: Nakagoryō, Furano, Hokkaido, Japan (New Furano Prince Hotel grounds)
P.w: About fifteen log-cabin craft shops linked by boardwalks in the Furano forest — silver snowflake charms, woodcarving, leather; lantern-lit after dark.

P.ad: Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan (former primary school)
P.w: Landscape photographer Shinzō Maeda's gallery of the Biei hills he made famous, in a converted primary school among birch groves.

P.n: Kawamura Kaneto Ainu Memorial Museum (川村カ子トアイヌ記念館)
P.ad: Hokumon-chō 11-chōme, Asahikawa, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Founded 1916 — Japan's oldest Ainu cultural museum, run by an Ainu family in the old Chikabumi kotan, with a reconstructed bamboo-grass cise house.

P.n: Hakuchō Ōhashi Bridge, Muroran (白鳥大橋)
P.ad: Muroran, Hokkaido, Japan (Route 37 across Muroran Port)
P.w: Eastern Japan's longest suspension bridge, spanning Muroran harbour — lit at night above the city's famous factory-night views.

F.n: Menya Saimi (麺屋彩未)
F.w: The miso-ramen counter Sapporo queues for — three white misos over a clear pork-bone broth, a dab of grated ginger on the chāshū. Michelin Bib Gourmand (Hokkaido 2017) and Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100 (2024).

F.n: Sumire Susukino (すみれ 札幌すすきの店)
F.ad: Pixis Bldg 2F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 3-9-2, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Murakami family house (1964) that codified the lard-sealed, scalding Sapporo miso bowl; the late-night Susukino branch pours the Nakanoshima honten broth. Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100 2024 & 2025.

F.n: MEN-EIJI Hiragishi Base (麺eiji 平岸base)
F.w: Additive-free broths and house-made noodles from Hokkaido wheat since 2006 — the gyokai-tonkotsu shōyu and the miso both draw lines. Michelin Bib Gourmand (Hokkaido 2017).

F.n: Jingisukan Daruma Honten (だるま本店)
F.ad: Crystal Bldg 1F, Minami 5-jō Nishi 4, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 064-0805, Japan
F.w: The Susukino jingisukan room since 1954 — a cast-iron dome at every seat, one cut of mutton, sweet-spicy dipping sauce, a queue from 17:30. Cash only.

F.n: Soup Curry Garaku (スープカレー GARAKU)
F.ad: Okumura Bldg B1F, Minami 2-jō Nishi 2-6-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Numbered tickets and daily lines for a soup curry whose broth borrows udon-shop dashi technique — pork bone and herbs stewed two days, kelp and bonito layered in.

F.n: Soup Curry & Dining Suage+ (すあげ+)
F.ad: Minami 4-jō Nishi (〒064-0804), Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan — a few minutes from Susukino Station
F.w: Locals' favourite Susukino soup curry: skewered roast chicken, stewed pork and a pile of local vegetables, with rice cut with red rice. 11:30–22:00 daily.

F.n: Oiso, Nijō Market (二条市場 大磯)
F.ad: Sapporo Nijō Market, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The classic first stop in 'Sapporo's kitchen' — morning queues for donburi of sea urchin, salmon roe and crab, ¥2,000–3,000.

F.n: Donburi Chaya, Nijō Market (どんぶり茶屋)
F.ad: Sapporo Nijō Market, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Born in Nijō Market, a specialist with over fifty kaisendon — all-crab, all-shrimp, uni-ikura-crab-scallop-botan-ebi — plus grilled-seafood bowls.

F.n: Rojiura Curry SAMURAI Sakura (路地裏カリィ侍. 櫻)
F.w: Rich soup curry built on vegetables contracted from farmers in Shibetsu and Nayoro — the 'Samurai' chain's original back-alley style.

F.n: Ajisai Honten, Hakodate (函館麺厨房あじさい 本店)
F.w: Founded 1930, the name in Hakodate shio ramen: a clear broth of southern-Dōnan kelp with pork and chicken bone and rock salt. Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100.

F.n: Lucky Pierrot Bay Area Honten (ラッキーピエロ ベイエリア本店)
F.ad: Bay Area waterfront, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Hakodate's own clown-themed burger chain (17 branches, all in the city) — the Chinese Chicken Burger, curry rice and soft-serve; the waterfront flagship.

F.n: Asahikawa Ramen Village (あさひかわラーメン村)
F.w: Eight of Asahikawa's best-known shops under one roof — the city's shōyu style: pork-bone and seafood double broth sealed under a film of lard, thin, firm, wavy noodles.

F.n: Ganso Butadon no Panchō, Obihiro (元祖豚丼のぱんちょう)
F.ad: In front of Obihiro Station, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The 1933 Obihiro shop credited with inventing butadon — sweet-soy charcoal-grilled pork on rice, the Tokachi soul food. The name is from the Chinese 'fan ting'.

F.n: Butadon no Tonta, Obihiro (ぶた丼のとん田)
F.w: Among Obihiro's most popular butadon counters; Michelin Bib Gourmand in the Hokkaido 2017 special edition.

F.n: Isezushi, Otaru (伊勢鮨)
F.w: Otaru's Michelin-starred sushi counter (Hokkaido guide one star), with a casual by-the-piece outpost inside Otaru Station.

F.n: Otaru Masazushi Honten (おたる政寿司 本店)
F.w: Founded 1938 on Otaru's Sushiya-dōri — the old guard of the city's sushi, as loved by locals as by visitors. 11:00–15:00, 17:00–21:00.

F.n: Soup Curry Picante, Kita 13-jō Honten (ピカンティ)
F.ad: Near Hokkaido University (Kita 13-jō), Kita-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: One of the founding soup-curry houses (1996), by Hokkaido University — vegetable-heavy curries with a choice of rich, light or shrimp-dashi broth.

F.n: Kushiro Washō Market (釧路和商市場)
F.w: Kushiro's 1954 indoor fish market of ~60 stalls, home of the katte-don — buy a bowl of rice, then walk the stalls choosing each topping.

F.n: Robata, Kushiro (炉ばた)
F.w: Seventy-plus years at the charcoal hearth in the city that claims to have invented robatayaki — counter seats only around the fire, fish grilled in front of you.

F.n: Sapporo Beer Garden (サッポロビール園)
F.ad: Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan (beside the Sapporo Beer Museum)
F.w: Restaurants spread through the garden serve fresh-lamb jingisukan and seasonal Hokkaido produce with Sapporo draught — Kessel Hall does all-you-can-eat-and-drink.

F.n: Ganso Sapporo Ramen Yokochō (元祖さっぽろラーメン横丁)
F.w: The narrow Susukino alley of a dozen-plus tiny ramen counters, open into the small hours — the classic post-drinking miso bowl.

F.n: Kitakaro Sapporo Honkan (北菓楼 札幌本館)
F.ad: Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan (3 min walk from Ōdōri Park)
F.w: Kitakaro's flagship in a historic building long loved as the city library and an art museum — sweets shop plus a café serving the cake set with Hokkaido-milk soft-serve.

F.n: Hasegawa Store Bay Area (ハセガワストア ベイエリア店)
F.w: Hakodate's convenience-store institution: the yakitori bentō grilled to order — in southern Hokkaido 'yakitori' means pork.

F.n: Uni Murakami Hakodate Honten (うに むらかみ 函館本店)
F.ad: Morning-market streets, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (5 min walk from Hakodate Station)
F.w: Restaurant of a sea-urchin wholesaler that long supplied Tsukiji and top sushi counters — sweet, additive-free raw uni in bowls and set meals.

F.n: Ramen Santouka Honten, Asahikawa (らーめん山頭火 本店)
F.w: Hitoshi Hatanaka's nine-seat 1988 shop that took Hokkaido ramen worldwide — a mild, low-salt white broth; the tokusei toroniku (pork-cheek) bowl.

F.n: Ramen no Hachiya Gojō Sōgyōten (ラーメンの蜂屋 五条創業店)
F.w: Since 1947: a pork-bone and dried-horse-mackerel double broth under burnt lard, with house noodles — the shop credited with Asahikawa's low-hydration noodle.

F.n: Baikōken Honten, Asahikawa (梅光軒 本店)
F.w: Founded 1969 — pork, chicken and seafood double broth, rich yet clean; first winner of the citizens' Asahikawa Ramen Grand Prize.

F.n: Obihiro Hageten Honten (帯広はげ天 本店)
F.w: Tempura and local-food house founded 1934, whose first chef Yano Shōroku helped devise the butadon sauce — marbled loin seared fast at high heat, a restrained sweet glaze.

F.n: Rokkatei Obihiro Main Store (六花亭 帯広本店)
F.w: The 1933 Tokachi confectioner's home store — the Marusei Butter Sandwich, crisp pies and assortments, with a second-floor kissa café.

F.n: Aji no Daiō Muroran Honten (味の大王 室蘭本店)
F.w: Serving its thick, rich curry ramen since opening in Muroran in 1971 — the bowl that made curry ramen the city's new local dish; house-made medium-thick curly noodles.
